root.label: Startup and termination
root.note: Static initialization, then dynamic initialization, then main, then a reverse teardown chosen by the exit path.

children.label: main
children.note: The program's entry point, with rules no other function has.

children.label: Declared int
children.note: Return type must be declared int; auto main() -> int is fine, deduction is not.

children.label: Forbidden forms
children.note: No inline, static, constexpr, consteval, deleted or coroutine main; it may not be used.

children.label: Implicit return 0
children.note: Falling off the end of main is equivalent to return 0.

children.label: Return calls exit
children.note: Returning destroys main's locals, then calls std::exit with the value.

children.label: Static initialization
children.note: Zero and constant initialization, complete before any dynamic initialization.

children.label: Constant init
children.note: Used when the initialization is a constant expression; safe to read from anywhere.

children.label: Zero init
children.note: Everything else with static storage is zeroed first.

children.label: constinit (C++20)
children.note: Requires constant initialization without making the variable const.

children.label: Static instead of dynamic
children.note: An implementation may do dynamic init statically, so early readers may see either value.

children.label: Dynamic initialization
children.note: Runs code; order depends on the kind of variable.

children.label: Ordered
children.note: Ordinary namespace-scope variables follow definition order within one file.

children.label: Partially ordered
children.note: Non-template inline variables keep the order they have in every defining file.

children.label: Unordered
children.note: Static members of class templates and variable template specializations have no order.

children.label: Deferral
children.note: May be deferred until first odr-use of something in the same file; implementation-defined.

children.label: Block statics
children.note: Initialized on first pass, thread-safe since C++11, retried if the initializer throws.

children.label: Exit paths
children.note: Each way out runs a different subset of the teardown.

children.label: std::exit
children.note: Thread-locals, then statics and atexit handlers in one reverse sequence, then C streams.

children.label: std::quick_exit
children.note: Only at_quick_exit handlers, in reverse, then _Exit; no objects destroyed.

children.label: std::abort
children.note: Abnormal termination; no destructors and no handlers of any kind.

children.label: std::terminate
children.note: Calls the terminate handler, abort by default; unwinding before it may not happen.

children.label: Teardown order
children.note: Reverse of completion, with atexit registrations in the same sequence.

children.label: Reverse completion
children.note: The static object constructed last is destroyed first.

children.label: atexit interleaving
children.note: A handler registered after an object completed runs before that object is destroyed.

children.label: Dead statics
children.note: Passing through a destroyed static local during later teardown is UB.

children.label: Exceptions
children.note: An exception from a static initializer, destructor or atexit handler calls terminate.
